Ben / team / Ledgerly NetOps — see answers & notes below (sending short, non-normative guidance for the POC):

PrivateLink vs VPC Peering (POC guidance):
- VPC Peering: higher throughput and lower per-request latency. Simpler for large egress volumes. Requires route table updates and cross-account peering acceptance in console. Works well if Ledgerly will own egress NAT.
- PrivateLink: easier security posture (interface endpoints), no cross-account route table changes, and better isolation. Slightly higher per-request latency for small payloads; scales well with many small clients. For ~500 RPS sustained, both are fine; for bursts to 2k RPS we recommend Peering unless you use multiple interface endpoints and scale the endpoint ENIs accordingly.

Redwood-managed egress for POC:
- We can offer a Redwood-managed static egress IP pool for the POC (limited, not recommended for long-term production without an SLA add-on). Operational notes: IPs are NAT through our edge; no additional cost other than a small provisioning fee for reserved IPs. If Ledgerly prefers, providing your own NAT IPs is simplest for production.

Minimal ports & CIDRs (destination):
- Dest ports: 443 (HTTPS) only.
- Destination CIDRs for Redwood-managed egress (POC): 34.201.120.0/26, 34.201.121.0/26 (sample / small set; final list will include regional CIDRs).
- If peering: no public CIDR needed; we'll provide private CIDR details in the alignment call.

Pre-call checklist (what we need from Ledgerly NetOps):
- Preferred connectivity option (Peering or PrivateLink).
- If Peering: VPC ID, account ID, two representative subnets (for routing), and any peer acceptance window.
- If PrivateLink: approved security policy for interface endpoints and whether TLS interception is present.
- Egress IPs (if Ledgerly-owned) or confirmation to accept Redwood-managed egress for the POC.
- A primary NetOps contact + preferred scheduling window (Mon/Tue mornings look best).

Attaching: a compact allowlist CSV and a 1-page network checklist (see attachments).

I’ll join the alignment call and bring our infra engineer if Ledgerly wants deeper packet/route review.
